ryan: Hey 👋 first-day setup question — I followed the onboarding README for dev env (Homebrew + dotfiles), but python 3.10 via pyenv isn't being picked up and npm global bins (like pnpm) aren't in my PATH. MacBook Pro (corporate, Intel). I added stuff to ~/.zshrc from the dotfiles repo but still getting 'python: command not found' when I try to run 'python3.10'. Any quick checks?

lena: welcome! :tada: Which dotfiles branch did you clone? we switched to using direnv + envrc to load project envs. also we recommend pyenv for python not system python.

ryan: I cloned https://git.redwood-inference/internal/dotfiles main branch and ran ./bootstrap. It symlinked .zshrc. My ~/.zshrc has these lines near the top: ```export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"\nsource "$HOME/.dotfiles/zsh/.zshrc"``` but no explicit pyenv init.

sam: ah — we moved away from pyenv init in favor of asdf for multi-runtime consistency. If you have asdf on PATH, run `asdf list` and `asdf current python` to see. If you installed pyenv earlier, there may be a PATH order issue.

ryan: running `asdf current python` prints nothing. `asdf list` returns empty. `which asdf` -> /usr/local/bin/asdf.

matt: ok two things: 1) Homebrew path for intel Macs is /usr/local not /opt/homebrew (that's for arm). ensure your brew did not end up in a different prefix. 2) after installing asdf you need to add its shims and completions. In zsh we add: ```# asdf\n. $(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh\n. $(brew --prefix asdf)/etc/profile.d/asdf.sh``` also add to PATH for npm globals: ```export NPM_PACKAGES="$HOME/.npm-global"\nexport PATH="$NPM_PACKAGES/bin:$PATH"```

ryan: I don't have /usr/local/Cellar — brew doctor says brew is installed in /opt/homebrew even though machine is intel? weird. Brew doctor suggests reinstall.

lena: hah that happens when users migrated configs. Try `which brew` and `brew --prefix`. If it's /opt/homebrew on intel, reinstall brew using the intel installer. But simpler: ensure the asdf reference uses `$(brew --prefix asdf)` which will resolve to whatever prefix your brew uses.

sam: also check that the dotfiles bootstrap added direnv hook in zsh: `eval "$(direnv hook zsh)"` and that you ran `direnv allow` in the repo root after cloning the project. direnv will populate PYENV_VERSION/ASDF envs.

ryan: quick logs: `which brew` -> /opt/homebrew/bin/brew, `brew --prefix asdf` -> /opt/homebrew/opt/asdf. After adding the two lines you suggested and restarting shell, `asdf list` is still empty. How do I install python 3.10 via asdf?

matt: `asdf plugin-add python` (only if not present) then `asdf install python 3.10.12` then `asdf global python 3.10.12` or `asdf local python 3.10.12` in a repo. if plugin exists run `asdf plugin-update --all` first. Also check `~/.tool-versions` to see pinned versions.

ryan: ran `asdf plugin-add python` -> plugin already present. `asdf install python 3.10.12` fails with `xx: python-build: no such release`.

lena: you might need openssl/xz dependencies: `brew install openssl readline xz zlib` then `export LDFLAGS` and `CPPFLAGS` pointing to brew --prefix openssl, for example: ```export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl)/lib"\nexport CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl)/include"\nasdf install python 3.10.12``` Also if install logs show a specific error paste it here.

ryan: OK installing deps now. Also npm global bins still not found after I added NPM_PACKAGES export; `echo $PATH` doesn't show ~/.npm-global/bin.

sam: ensure you exported NPM_PACKAGES before npm config set prefix is run. You can run: `mkdir -p "$HOME/.npm-global" && npm config set prefix "$HOME/.npm-global"` then add `export PATH="$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"` to ~/.zshrc and restart shell.

ryan: did `npm config set prefix` and `which pnpm` still points to /usr/local/bin/pnpm (leftover). I uninstalled global pnpm and reinstalled `npm i -g pnpm`. Now `which pnpm` -> /Users/ryan/.npm-global/bin/pnpm. yay.

matt: awesome. one pro tip: run `command -v python3.10` and `python3.10 --version` after asdf install. If you still get /usr/bin/python use `asdf which python` to see shim path. If path resolution still wrong, check ordering in .zshrc so that asdf shims come before /usr/bin.

ryan: after deps and install, `python3.10 --version` -> Python 3.10.12. asdf current shows 3.10.12. dotfiles direnv loads .envrc? I had to run `direnv allow` in the repo. All good now. Thanks everyone! :raised_hands:

devops-bot: Note: ticket #INF-423 created to track docs update: add intel vs arm brew notes to onboarding README. Assigned to @lena.

lena: I'll pick up that doc update. ping me if you find other edgecases.

ryan: Thanks — appreciate the fast help. I'll leave a short PR to the dotfiles README about npm prefix ordering.
